chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about the work of the ruler (tax farming/levy) in which a man engages; he said: 'It is permissible unless he is unable to do anything, nor can he eat or drink, nor can he find a way out; if he does so and something comes into his hand, let him send its khums to the Ahl al-Bayt.'

key_terms.عَمَلِ السُّلْطَانِ: Work of the ruler (tax farming or administrative duties)
key_terms.يَخْرُجُ فِيهِ: Engages in it / proceeds in it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on working for the ruler or in their domain according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling on working for the political authority (al-Sultan), permitting it as a necessity when one cannot sustain themselves or find alternative means. It establishes that any wealth acquired in this capacity is subject to khums, which must be remitted to the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the Shia view of financial accountability even in service to rulers. This ruling underscores the practical application of khums in socio-political contexts, ensuring that those serving the state remain spiritually and financially connected to the Imams.
